posts.text: libghostty for Rust! Some Ghostty maintainers came together and made a really high quality Rust crate in front of libghostty-vt. The repo includes a full port of Ghostling (full terminal in a single Rust file!). The API is beautiful.
posts.notes: libghostty-rs: high-quality Rust crate wrapping libghostty-vt. Full Ghostling port in a single Rust file. 68K views, 337 bookmarks. Signals libghostty cross-language maturity -- Rust binding unlocks agentic tools that want terminal emulation in Rust (relevant for cmux-adjacent projects and any Rust-based orchestrator work).

posts.text:
Ghostty 1.3 is going to have a preview of AppleScript support. All windows, tabs, splits, terminals are exposed via AppleScript. For macOS users, this satisfies some of the most common requests: broadcast commands, automatic layouts, jump to working directory, etc. PR here: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/pull/11208

I also think this is an incredibly important feature to ship early/now so agentic tools like Claude and Codex can take advantage of a scriptable Ghostty on macOS.
posts.notes: Ghostty 1.3 AppleScript preview. Explicitly motivated by enabling Claude/Codex agentic control. Broadcast commands, automatic layouts, jump to working dir. 179K views. Strong signal: terminal-level scriptability as agentic infrastructure.

posts.text: Ghostty 1.3 is now out! Scrollback search, native scrollbars, click-to-move cursor, rich clipboard copy, AppleScript, split drag/drop, Unicode 17 and international text improvements, massive performance improvements, and hundreds more changes.
posts.notes: Ghostty 1.3 official release announcement. 324K views, 584 bookmarks. AppleScript, scrollback search, split drag/drop. Release notes at ghostty.org.

posts.text: With Ghostty 1.3 out the door, my focus is now on completing the libghostty C API (Zig API is already complete). Just added the groundwork for exposing full terminal state and formatting it as plain text, VT, or HTML.
posts.notes: libghostty C API development progress post. Terminal state exposure as plain text/VT/HTML — key for programmatic agent control. Zig API already complete.

posts.text: Another example of libghostty bettering our core is that Ghostty GUI only supports 64-bit Mac+Linux+FreeBSD. But libghostty supports 32 and 64-bit, Windows, Android, and many other systems. Every time we add a new C API, our CI coverage expands to ensure more of Ghostty's core
posts.notes: libghostty cross-platform advantage post: supports 32/64-bit, Windows, Android vs Ghostty GUI (64-bit Mac/Linux only). CI coverage expands with each new C API. Signals libghostty as the truly universal terminal core.

posts.text: @h1th3sh cmux uses libghostty and is a perfect example of what Ghostty is trying to achieve (enabling other terminals). It's a huge success story and there is nothing for us to catch up to. Everyone going to cmux or another libghostty terminal instead of Ghostty would be great.
posts.notes: Direct endorsement of cmux as the exemplar libghostty success. mitchellh explicitly blessing the cmux ecosystem. Low engagement (reply), but high quote value.

posts.text: From empty repo to a functional minimal standalone terminal based on libghostty in 2 hours, presenting Ghostling! ~600 lines of C and you get extremely accurate, performant, and proven terminal emulation.
posts.notes: Ghostling demo: 600-line C program → full terminal in 2 hours using libghostty. Proof of concept for the libghostty API. 108K views, 359 bookmarks. Signal: low barrier to building terminals on libghostty foundation.
